correctness.rationale: The complete finite class is determined by the dominance and deletion tests, and a second neighborhood-transversal enumerator agrees for every order one through eleven. Exact VC checking exhausts all 462 five-vertex candidate sets on the eleven-vertex path and supplies all 16 traces on a four-vertex witness set. A verified complete 32-leaf depth-five tree and the 36-hypothesis count prove Ldim=5. All smaller paths have verified equal dimensions. The product decomposition and inductive Ldim product lemma prove both dimensions for arbitrary positive component counts; there is no infinite extrapolation from data.

evidence: Guingona et al. (arXiv:2109.04805) prove VC=Ldim for zero sets of linear combinations; no linear zero-set realization of this minimal-dominator class follows from their stated assumptions. A fixed-cardinality edge-matching construction on disjoint paths gives a different gap but does not calculate minimal-dominator incidence dimensions.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither equality for linear zero sets nor an example using exact-cardinality edge matchings implies the claimed first separation for inclusion-minimal vertex dominating sets, although generic VC<=Ldim and product additivity are well known.

evidence: Minimal dominating sets are exactly minimal transversals of the closed-neighborhood hypergraph; this equivalence was used in the alternative enumeration. Mofidi (2022) studies dominating-graph median properties, not VC/Littlestone of its minimal-dominator vertex sets. Mary (2024) uses VC bounds on the input hypergraph in an enumeration result; only the abstract was available for comparison.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Recasting the concept family as minimal transversals or private-neighbor incidence does not itself provide the eleven-vertex values; no inspected result with that conclusion was found. Exact opposite-concept or coordinate duality reductions were considered: the query domain is the vertices, and the hypotheses are minimal dominating sets, not graph-neighborhood hypotheses.

originality.rationale: The fully specified minimal-dominator vertex-membership class has a finite first path cutoff and a quantitatively exact product gap. Searches and material inspections found related domination/transversal enumeration, zero-set dimensions, and a distinct matching-edge gap, but no result that yields the 36-hypothesis VC=4 and Ldim=5 base. The novelty assessment is best-knowledge and not an assertion of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: Unindexed, differently named or unpublished computations of the same minimal-dominator path set system could exist.
The full manuscript of arXiv:2407.00694 was not inspected; the narrower semantic distinction follows only from its abstract.
Additivity is a general standard property and not independently original; priority depends on the finite minimal-dominator base and its first occurrence.

value.rationale: Inclusion-minimal dominating sets form a canonical family of minimal graph solutions and closed-neighborhood transversals. The sharp first graph order where ordinary and adaptive vertex-membership shattering separate is a motivated natural cutoff. The verified base produces a precisely quantified linear, unbounded gap on degree-two forests, complementing—but not implied by—prior matching-edge examples. The result is a finite structural benchmark plus an infinite family rather than a merely renamed textbook identity.
